inspection_method: headless-rendered blueprint screenshot opened with the image reader and read panel by panel; every observation is something visible in the image, not an inference from the JSON
observations: top-left panel 'final pile (static copy) + tool + contacts': a broad grey mound of pellets fills the lower half; each pellet is drawn as a rosette of several overlapping spheres (the 7-sphere lens clump), so the clump geometry survived the whole scoop and the settled random orientations are visible

above the mound, the final tool pose is drawn as two green ring outlines (fixed bowl + door shells, static copy, lifted ~80 mm); inside the rings sits a compact orange cluster (= in-cavity, captured pellets, 154 clumps) with light-blue pellets (= carried-by-height but outside the cavity) packed at the mouth on the door side

a string of light-blue/grey pellets hangs below the mouth and continues down toward the mound: pellets are leaking through the 9.9 mm lip gap (door stopped at the 4.94 deg floor) and are in flight at the final frame — this is the direct visual explanation for the low fill (0.124) and for the 80 mm spikes that the resting-particle post-processing removes

at the default time cursor (+0.9 s, descend phase) the descend-time tool is also drawn lower down: green fixed ring and blue door ring resting on the pile crown with a band of red contact points along the lip where it presses the pellets — so tool/contact geometry is time-resolved in the RRD and matches the z_lip curve

top-right panel 'post heightmap + crater azimuths/fit rings': the 5 mm post heightmap point grid is coloured cyan (low) to red (high) and shows a single broad hill; four white arrows radiate from the crater centre labelled '+x 16.3deg', '+y 42.6deg', '-x 13.4deg', '-y nandeg', with small red fit-ring markers on the +x/+y/-x arms

bottom-left 'Float64 metrics': z_lip_mm (orange) descends linearly from ~51 to ~16 mm over 0-2 s, holds during closure, then rises linearly to ~97 mm by 2.56 s; q_deg (green) drops from 27.5 to 5.0 between ~1.5 s and 2.0 s and stays flat at 5 (floor); lipF_N (yellow) stays near 0 with small bumps up to ~2 N near 2.0 s — no force spike, consistent with no stall and no divergence

bottom-right 'decision events': four INFO rows at +2.00/+2.54/+2.56 s: DOOR_STOP close q=4.988 reason=door_floor M=0.2276; DOOR_STOP reclose q=4.943 door_floor M=0.1171; CAPTURE n_in_cavity=154 mass_g=3.1196 fill_vs_bulk=0.1241 carried_z=210 diverged=False; CRATER_ANGLE_deg +x=16.3 +y=42.6 -x=13.4 -y=None center_mm=[1.0,-6.7] removed_cm3=35.39 (report only, not a verdict)
limitations_seen_in_the_image: the crater depression itself is hard to read in the heightmap panel from this camera angle (the hill top is red and the dip is only a paler patch); the matplotlib heightmap_seed460.png / heightmap_rest_seed460.png is the clearer view of the crater
azimuth labels overlap near the crater centre; the -y arm shows 'nandeg' because that wall spans a single 5 mm ring in the 20-80 % depth band (steep, unresolved on the grid)

the static final-tool copy and the time-cursor tool are drawn together, which is intended but can be mistaken for two tools; the 0.9 s cursor is the headless viewer default, not a chosen decision time
pile colours: pre-scoop pile (spheres_pre at t=0) is not shown at this cursor; only the final static copy is visible
the crater angles shown in the RRD are the original result-JSON values (before the resting-particle post-processing); the rest-only values (+y 38.1, others equal) are in crater_rest_seed460.json
